SRC-044:R11.text: [PERF-001] separate "preserve sole audit content" from "keep every conversation in the hot metadata index". Enforce a hard bounded metadata index on every update, not only after complete runs. Never delete pending/failed/incomplete wave blobs merely to satisfy that metadata bound: evict only their old summary/index entry, because revisiting or writing that conversation can reconstruct its summary from its still-present per-wave storage. Keep the existing completed-history policy for actual wave-blob deletion. Prefer a compact per-conversation wave-status summary so updating one record does not need to parse full audit texts merely to derive complete/pending/failed. Avoid rewriting the global index when the resulting compact metadata bytes are unchanged.

SRC-044:R12.text: [PERF-002] make the cheap facts cheap first. Track the last observed pathname/conversation route and avoid full runtime rebinding when a topology mutation cannot have changed route or authentication state. Compute `authVisible` once per probe and pass it into root-quarantine derivation rather than rescanning. Coalesce root/auth discovery to one trailing probe per topology burst, while allowing explicit route changes or mutations that introduce/remove likely auth-modal/login controls to invalidate that probe immediately. Keep attachment and conversation-turn mutation handling scoped to the actual changed nodes rather than coupling those mutations to global auth scans.

SRC-044:R13.text: [PERF-003] centralize worker removal in one helper that removes the worker and its `worker:<id>` reload-dedup entry, and use it for expiry, offline registration, duplicate-slot retirement, capacity eviction and every other current `_workers.pop` path. If some short post-removal memory is required, use an explicit bounded TTL/LRU rather than immortal entries.

SRC-044:R14.text: [PERF-004] preserve `read_inbox_cached()` immediate-change semantics for callers that require them. Optimize the passive dashboard layer instead: maintain a bounded per-project next-probe/invalidation record so a 4-second UI repaint does not necessarily force another physical inbox scan before its configured freshness budget expires; force an immediate physical probe before any operator action whose correctness depends on the inbox verdict and when a known project/audit-inbox change invalidates it. Independently bound the module cache with an LRU/project-registry-aware eviction policy. Within `_inbox_fingerprint()`, use a lower-overhead directory enumeration/stat path where available, but do not rely solely on coarse directory mtime because the existing Windows same-tick contract explicitly rejects that.

SRC-044:R15.text: [PERF-005] keep the GUI-thread chokepoint but make its timer lifecycle match pack lifecycle. Start the 250 ms timer on the GUI thread when the first pack enters PACKING; keep one timer while any individual/sequential/auto-pack operation is active; after the final buffered snapshot is flushed and no pack task remains, stop it. An equivalent queued Qt signal that arms one coalesced single-shot flush is acceptable, provided worker threads never manipulate Qt objects directly.
